fieldNotes: Planar body model (sagittal plane). Segment lengths are fractions of height; mass fractions of body mass.
Proportions after Winter, Biomechanics and Motor Control of Human Movement (4th ed.), Table 4.1. Head and trunk radii of gyration are approximations.
com: centre of mass along the segment, as a fraction of its length from the proximal joint. gyration: radius of gyration about the segment's own centre of mass, as a fraction of its length.
paired segments (arms, legs) are listed once and counted twice.
foot: modelled as the heel height below the ankle, along the shank (pointed toes).
Joint angles in degrees: shoulder 0 = arms down, 180 = overhead; elbow and knee 0 = straight; hip 0 = legs straight down, positive = legs forward (towards the chest).
shapeChangeTime: seconds to go from straight to full tuck; every joint moves at the same angular speed.
radius: segment thickness as a fraction of height (a cylinder of that radius), used for the moment of inertia about the long axis (twist) and for the figure's visuals.
shoulderHalfWidth, hipHalfWidth: distance of the shoulder and hip joints from the body's midline, as a fraction of height.
handsIn (pose): 0 = hands at shoulder width, 1 = hands at the midline (arms on the chest).

twist: maxTurnsPerSecond is the twist rate in the 'twist' pose (straight body, arms on the chest); other shapes twist slower because their inertia about the long axis is larger. spinUpTime / stopTime: seconds to reach full twist speed after pressing, and to stop after letting go.
